paper.title_en: Reciprocal Darboux-square duality for non-null curves in Lorentz–Minkowski 3-space
paper.abstract_en: •Reciprocal Darboux-square normalization gives an involutive Lorentzian curve lift.•Null-boundary curvature blow-up and endpoint regularity are characterized.•Exact finite-switching detector-kernel equality is classified in 2+1 dimensions.•A Schwarzian defect quantifies failure of the controlled response comparison.•Rindler spectra and cross-kernel counterexamples delimit the physical scope. We study a reciprocal normalization of positive Combescure pairs in Lorentz–Minkowski three-space and its finite-time detector consequences. Relative to a fixed reference length, the scale <math altimg="si33.svg"><mrow><mi>ρ</mi><mo linebreak="goodbreak">=</mo><mo>|</mo><mi>Q</mi><mo>|</mo></mrow></math>, with <math altimg="si34.svg"><mrow><mi>Q</mi><mo linebreak="goodbreak">=</mo><mo>〈</mo><mi>W</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>W</mi><mo>〉</mo><mo>≠</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></math>, sends the Lorentzian Darboux square to <math altimg="si35.svg"><msup><mi>Q</mi><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math> and defines an involutive curve lift up to translation. General Combescure connection preservation and stationary massless-detector scaling serve as background, not as new field-theoretic symmetries. At a one-sided zero of order p > 0 of Q, the image has an integrable curvature singularity of order <math altimg="si36.svg"><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo linebreak="goodbreak">/</mo><mo>(</mo><mi>p</mi><mo linebreak="goodbreak">+</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow></math> and a C<sup loc="post">1</sup>, but no Frenet-regular C<sup loc="post">2</sup>, endpoint extension. For smooth timelike curves in the <math altimg="si2.svg"><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo linebreak="goodbreak">+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></math>-dimensional massless Minkowski vacuum, we specify a driven two-level detector comparison with image gap Ω/ρ and interaction envelope weighted by <math altimg="si37.svg"><msup><mi>ρ</mi><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></math>. We classify exact equality of its finite-switching response kernels: either Q is constant, or curvature and torsion have the inverse-proper-time form <math altimg="si38.svg"><mrow><mrow><mi>κ</mi><mo linebreak="badbreak">=</mo><mi>a</mi><mo linebreak="badbreak">/</mo><mo>|</mo><mi>s</mi><mo linebreak="badbreak">−</mo></mrow><msub><mi>s</mi><mi>c</mi></msub><mrow><mo>|</mo></mrow></mrow></math>, <math altimg="si39.svg"><mrow><mrow><mi>τ</mi><mo linebreak="badbreak">=</mo><mi>b</mi><mo linebreak="badbreak">/</mo><mo>|</mo><mi>s</mi><mo linebreak="badbreak">−</mo></mrow><msub><mi>s</mi><mi>c</mi></msub><mrow><mo>|</mo></mrow></mrow></math>, with a<sup loc="post">2</sup> ≠ b<sup loc="post">2</sup>. The Schwarzian derivative of the proper-time map controls the leading local kernel defect and, where nonzero, gives a nonzero short-switching response difference for sufficiently short nonnegative pulses. The driven comparison is independent of the reference scale only when the detector driving is changed consistently; an unchanged apparatus is not claimed to be invariant. Explicit Rindler spectra distinguish <math altimg="si2.svg"><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo linebreak="goodbreak">+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></math> from <math altimg="si3.svg"><mrow><mn>3</mn><mo linebreak="goodbreak">+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></math> dimensions. Two-detector and modified-dispersion comparisons delimit the scope of the single-detector result rather than assert its robustness.
